Nevertheless, as discussed in [15] , what is right for two patches may not be necessarily
right for three patches or more. The presence of a third host may indeed cause a springboard
effect, leading to higher chances of persistence of the pathogen, compared to an environment
with two hosts. This is a common pattern in zoonoses. For instance the main reservoirs of
influenza A virus are the aquatic birds, but it is widely accepted that these viruses need to
adapt in an intermediate host (such as pig or poultry) before they lead to an outbreak in
human populations [21, 25] . Coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2, are
also zoonotic, with bats as presumed main reservoir. Intermediate hosts are also suspected
to have played an important role in the 2003 and 2019 outbreaks [13, 14] .
